scope: 25 whole uncertainty records inspected; exact integrated parent retention remains pending.
additional_source_basis: Prior complete source-first/current-record and auxiliary rereads of171,182–183,201–205,210–219,221–245; exact density policy and scope disposition.

rows.review_disposition: 192–193 ground Valmy in superior French guns, numbers and patriotic fighting, followed by Goethe’s attributed new-epoch interpretation. Opaque first/second shorthand must be replaced with those distinct formulations.

Saint-Domingue slave revolt, metropolitan reactions, free-coloured citizenship, continued slavery and subsequent emancipation are distinct political/legal phases; priority must preserve their different demands rather than count aliases as substitutes.
182 Pont-Saint-Esprit is a concrete instance of rumor-driven regional violence. A named event facet can preserve retrieval within the larger qualified explanation without a duplicate weighted parent.
Chunk ownership is administrative. Retire the asserted reconciliation status; final Valmy and later-war records must independently fulfil their exact content.

197 is about Gustavus III, noble assassins and the displacement of responsibility onto Jacobinism. Geoffrey Parker does not appear. Correct the unsupported named analogy and bind Gustavus’s substantive 171/197 treatment.
204/206–207 distinguish Hondschoote, Wattignies and Tourcoing from the decisive Fleurus turning point. Consolidation must retain each useful event route and the hierarchy of significance.
The Vendée and Quiberon references connect foreign war to domestic counterrevolution. Their fuller later treatment does not license losing the military consequences here.
Campaign success, unilateral peace design, dependent republics and intervention in French politics are distinct mechanisms in Bonaparte’s rise, despite their linked narrative.
219 explicitly makes war an engine of radicalization. Preserve that interpretation through the specified emergency mechanisms and their chronology, not a second generic war survey.
206–207 distinguish a tactically damaged French fleet from the successful grain-convoy objective. This is a concrete naval qualification; blockade/maritime limitation alone would not preserve it.

Belgian aspirations, natural-frontier annexation and subsequent occupation/governance concern different actors, political ends and phases; all must remain independently retrievable where substantively treated.
British reform, loyalism/repression, war entry and strategic/financial pressures have distinct explanatory content. Separate requirements are justified by meaning, not the number of labels.
February’s levy of 300,000 and August’s levée en masse differ in scope, decree and effects. Preserve the distinction rather than treating their names as equivalents.
Unavailable endnotes cannot resolve attribution. Replace the fragmentary instruction with a bounded source-availability rule; no unsupported reconstruction or external edition is part of this review.
221/241–242 reject national dismemberment as the rebels’ common aim. Hostile Federalist terminology requires qualification; republican local autonomy coexists with divergent royalist participation.

241 contrasts June alarm/claims of60–70 departments with an administrator’s31July observation of serious resistance in eight. Preserve dates, criteria and perspectives, not two equivalent disputed counts.
235 gives a wide National Guard estimate and additional onlookers. Coercion and encirclement are secure without a precise force size.
235–236 explicitly reject a party/government model and describe overlapping circles, divergent votes and late coordination under threat. Retain useful grouping access without a fixed roster.
246 distinguishes an official affirmative total from the author’s probable higher estimate. Neither should silently replace the other.
241 asserts Wimpffen’s royalism but hedges English pay. Distinguish those evidentiary strengths rather than treating both as speculation or both as established.
Qualified republican/local-autonomy meaning must survive consolidation; royalist participation is a separate source-supported complication, not the definition of the whole movement.
235–236 directly reject disciplined-party and government interpretations. Preserve the analytic rejection, not merely a renamed group.
Endnotes remain unavailable/excluded; retain the limitation without letting it disqualify complete main-text arguments.

Density measurement is administrative metadata, already governed by the exact density basis and source-scope disposition. Retire this semantic uncertainty and bind the clean scope-corrected measurement during final integration.

Provincial revolt has distinct city causes, anti-centralization claims, fiscal/social conflicts, Girondin repression and royalist participation. Preserve those differences rather than a single party conspiracy explanation.
